notes:
DUPLICATE-COMPANY DETERMINATION (per brief flag vs S.N. 78 'Ferm Living US', c78.json): genuinely SEPARATE catalogue, NOT a duplicate. Evidence: (1) fermliving.com resolves to Shopify shop 'fermliving-com.myshopify.com' (shopId 15033368640, countryCode DK, currencyCode EUR) - a completely different Shopify instance from the US site (fermliving.us, its own myshopify store). (2) The site's own country/currency switcher on fermliving.com lists FOUR separate country domains as distinct stores: 'United States / USD' -> fermliving.us, 'United Kingdom / GBP' -> fermliving.co.uk, 'Denmark / DKK' -> fermliving.com (current), 'Sweden / SEK' -> fermliving.se - confirming Ferm Living runs multiple independent country/region Shopify storefronts, of which fermliving.com is the Denmark/EU one (hreflang alternates also show fermliving.com carries locale sub-paths for nl-NL/de-DE/fr-FR/es-ES, i.e. it is the broader EU hub store, separate again from fermliving.dk which appears as its own hreflang-alternate domain). (3) Product catalogue is materially larger/different: fermliving.com's nav (mega-menu, live-checked via data-dynamic-menu-parent attributes) exposes Furniture, Sofas, Rugs and Textiles as fully public top-level nav branches (all excluded here per category-type rules, but present and browsable), which on the US site's live nav were either absent or only reachable as orphaned unmenued collections. This matches the S.N. 138 Anthropologie-UK-style outcome (bare domain = genuinely distinct site), not the S.N. 137/142/151/153/156/159/161/164/165/166/168-style literal duplicate outcome. Extracted independently, rows NOT skipped.

NETWORK/ACCESS NOTE (important for count accuracy): direct fetch of fermliving.com worked throughout, no WAF. However, the storefront resolves a Shopify Markets context by request geo-IP; this session's default geo resolved to India ('Shopify.country="IN"' seen in page JS), and under that market context /collections/<handle>/products.json returned severely deflated results for ALL Lighting collections (e.g. portable-lamps 0, floor-lamps 5, table-lamps 7, wall-lamps 1) while non-electrical decor collections (mirrors, vases, kitchenware) were unaffected - evidently Ferm Living restricts electrical/lamp SKUs from markets outside their supported plug/certification regions. Fix: requested https://fermliving.com/?country=DK once to set the Shopify 'localization=DK' cookie (matching this company's assigned roster country), then re-ran full-pagination product-ID-exhaustion counts (limit=250, looped to an empty page, de-duplicated by unique numeric product ID) against every handle under that DK market session. All resulting counts then matched the /collections.json 'products_count' field exactly for every handle checked (20+ handles cross-verified), confirming both the DK-market pagination method and the products_count field are reliable and mutually consistent here - this is the correct, non-deflated true catalogue count for the Denmark/EU store.

Rule 0 applications: kept 'Kids Lamps' (22) as a Lighting sub-category despite site nav filing it under the 'Kids' menu - product type is a lamp fixture, not audience-based exclusion. Kept 'Outdoor Pots' (40) alongside 'Plant Pots' (58) per Rule 0.6 - a genuine room-based nav branch (Outdoor Living menu) distinct from the type-based Accessories>Plant Pots branch, overlap not de-duplicated (consistent with c78's identical finding on the sibling US site).

EXCLUDED after title inspection: 'Candles' (49: mix of Dryp/Pure/Mura/Burren/Stala unscented lines plus explicitly 'Scented Candle' items e.g. Rylith, Ura, Kurinu, Vitto) - same as c78's US finding, unscented items have no dedicated listing URL of their own separate from the mixed collection, so the whole node was dropped rather than fabricating a filtered count. 'Outdoor Accessories' (63) - inspected all titles: majority are furniture seat cushions/pads/protective covers (Dapple Cushion/Seat Pad x12, Desert Protective Cover/Lounge Seat x9, Rouli covers x2, Outdoor Seat Pad), umbrellas (Lull x3), garden tools/bags/toolboxes (Bark bags/apron/wall storage x5, Grib Toolbox x2, Antila Watering Can); genuine decor items (door knockers, water globes, fire pits, a bird feeder, lantern, sculptural piece, candle holder, wall boxes, 2 portable lamps) are a minority with no clean sub-URL to isolate - dropped as a non-decor-majority mixed roll-up, matching c78's identical finding on this same collection type. 'Kids Accessories' (49) - inspected titles: contains Wallpaper (3: Katie Scott, Dot, The Park - explicit exclusion), Textile Maps (2), Bed Canopy (2), Clothes Hangers (1), Pencil Wrap (1) mixed in with no dedicated sub-URL to strip them from the otherwise-decorative majority (hooks, hand-carved animal hooks, money banks, plant pots) - dropped rather than padding, consistent with c78's identical determination on this collection. 'Baby' / baby-objects (31) - inspected titles: baby furniture (cot, changing unit, dresser, high chair) and soft-goods/toys (blankets, mobiles, soft toys, quilted mats, playmats) - not a decor category at all, standard furniture/textile/toy exclusions apply, dropped entirely (this collection did not exist as a separate node on the US site). 'Certified Products' (529) and 'Certified Kids Products' (214) - verified by sample: a sustainability-certification facet cutting across Furniture, Textiles, Kitchen and other already-distinct categories (sample pull showed Atura Dining Table, Ekko Towels, Grova Side Table, Sen Cushion Cover, Kiru Carafe, Boda Dining Chair together) - a cross-cutting facet re-cut, not a genuine product-type category, dropped per facet rule. 'Spare Parts' (47) and 'Gift Sets' (30, Holiday & Gift exclusion) - standard exclusions, not inspected further as clearly out of scope by name/type. Standard exclusions applied without further inspection: Kitchen Textiles, Kitchen Tools and Utensils, Wallpaper (top-level, 4), all Furniture-menu collections (Outdoor Furniture, Lounge Chairs, Poufs, Daybeds, Tables, Chairs and Benches, Stools, Storage, Shelves, Fabric Samples), all Sofas-menu collections (2/3/4-seaters, Rico/Catena/Dase modules and sofas, Turn Sofas), all Textiles-menu collections (Cushions, Cushion Covers, Bedspreads and Throws, Towels, Shower Curtains), all Rugs-menu collections (Rectangular Rugs, Round Rugs, Mats and Runners), all Kids-menu non-lighting collections (Toys, Textiles, Storage, Furniture, Rugs, Wallpaper), all Outdoor Living non-pot collections (Outdoor Textiles, Outdoor Seating, Outdoor Tables - furniture), and all marketing/editorial nav items (All X roll-ups, News, Kids News, Bestsellers, Ferm Living Classics, Shop by Series, Gift Guides, the 'Customise your own lamp'/'Customise your own shelving system'/'Design your own [Sofa]' configurator pages, all 'The [Room]' and 'The [Room] see what is coming' lifestyle/lookbook pages, blogs/pages/stories content).

Kept with minor documented contamination (same pattern as c78): 'Hooks and Holders' (57) - majority decorative wall hooks/coat racks; 8 items (Dora Towel Shelf x3, Dora/Curvature Toilet Paper Holder x5) are bathroom plumbing-adjacent hardware with no separate URL to strip out. 'Small Storage' (150) - dominated by decorative trays/bowls/baskets/centrepieces/jars/desk accessories plus the decorative ceramic 'Mist' bathroom-accessory line (soap dishes/toothbrush holders/tissue boxes - decorative, in scope under Rule 0.4); ~5 items (Port Toolbox/Firewood Bucket/Kindling and Ash Bucket/Fireplace Tools/Wood Basket) are fireplace-utility contamination.
